# .github — notes for Claude

`workflows/build.yml` (tests, headless UI tests on Linux, OWASP Dependency-Check (`dependency-check`: CVSS ≥ 7 fails, false positives in `dependency-check-suppressions.xml` each with its `<notes>`), LottieConverter cross-built for Windows (`lottie-windows`, MinGW-w64 on Linux, handed to the Windows job), packages, releases on a `v<version>` tag), `workflows/natives.yml` (what has no official build) and `workflows/codeql.yml` (CodeQL's `security-and-quality` with `build-mode: none`, any result without a suppression fails). Dependency-Check runs in CI only, never locally (the NVD database fills the disk); CodeQL runs in CI, and by hand when checking its findings (below), never in the build. Packaging and signing: `packaging/CLAUDE.md`.

- Token permissions: `contents: read` at the top, `write` only in the job that publishes. Jobs that build third-party code (cargo, go) run their build scripts with the token, so they never get write, and checkouts use `persist-credentials: false`.
- No `${{ … }}` inside `run:` with values that could come from outside (PR titles, branch names, matrix values from files): pass them through `env:`.
- Actions are pinned by their commit's full SHA with the tag in a comment (`uses: actions/checkout@<40 hex> # v5.1.0`), read with `git ls-remote --tags <repo>` (an annotated tag's commit is its `^{}` line). `WorkflowRulesTest` reads every workflow and fails on an action pinned otherwise, a `${{` inside a `run:`, a workflow without `contents: read` at the top, and a suppression without its reason.
- CodeQL: a finding is fixed, or suppressed on its own line, `// lgtm[java/rule] why` at the line's end, or on one member, `@SuppressWarnings("lgtm[java/rule]") // why` (never a type, never the bare mark, which is every rule; the `codeql[...]` mark, which works on the line below, isn't used). Those count only because `codeql.yml` runs `codeql/alert-suppression.qls` (CodeQL's own `AlertSuppression.ql` and `AlertSuppressionAnnotations.ql`) beside `security-and-quality`, which doesn't include them. `SuppressionsHaveReasonsTest` makes each say why. A rule that is noise for the whole code is left out only in a config file's `query-filters` (`config-file:`), one `exclude` by `id` each with its reason in a comment above it; `WorkflowRulesTest` checks both. None is left out today.
- CodeQL runs locally too, without the full bundle (~880 MB, 2.5 GB unpacked): stream the macOS bundle through `zstd -dc | tar -x`, leaving out the other languages' extractors and packs but keeping `xml` (the Java extractor and `java-all` need it), then `codeql database create --language=java --build-mode=none` on a copy of the tracked files only (an ignored `.worktrees/` or `target/` adds findings CI never sees) and `codeql database analyze` with `codeql/java-queries:codeql-suites/java-security-and-quality.qls` and the suppression suite. The gate's `jq` on the SARIF gives what CI would say.

## Lessons
- `natives.yml` pasted `${{ matrix.bridge.* }}` (read from `versions.env`) and other matrix values into `run:` scripts: a crafted value became shell code. They go through `env:` and are used as `"$VAR"`; check with `grep -n '\${{' .github/workflows/*.yml` that none is left inside a `run:`.
- `ui-headless` blocks the build and the release (since 2026-11-10). It was informative and failed on every run for days without anyone seeing it: `ComposerHeightUiTest`'s sentence still took two lines at 704 px with Linux's wider font. A test's failure message saying what it measured (its sizes) is what found it from CI alone.
- CodeQL's first run had 99 findings, and the `// lgtm[...]` marks would have done nothing: `security-and-quality` doesn't include the suppression queries, so the SARIF had no `suppressions` for the gate to read. Checked by running the bundle's CLI on the code, before and after (`codeql.yml` now runs `alert-suppression.qls`).
- `smoke-windows` checked each bridge with `"./$f.exe" -e -c … && test -s …` inside a `for` loop: under `bash -e` a failure on the left of `&&` doesn't stop the script, so a bridge that can't write its config (the legacy Discord one has no `-e`) passed. Each check is a command of its own, and the files it doesn't apply to are named (`mautrix-discord-*`), never guessed from their `-h` text (a help that prints differently would skip the check in silence).
